slides.title: O maior, o menor
slides.text: Superlativos têm 'the': the tallest, the most beautiful. O Everest é 'the highest mountain in the world'. O rio Amazonas é 'the longest river' em volume. Quase todo ranking usa essa forma.
Nora e Sven olham fotos da cordilheira e conversam sobre os picos.
slides.line: What's the highest mountain in the photo?

slides.title: The mountain book
slides.text: Nora has a big book about mountains. The highest mountain is in Asia: Mount Everest. The most popular mountain is in the Alps. The oldest mountain range is in Africa. The coldest one is in Antarctica. The most beautiful one, in Nora's opinion, is the small mountain near her grandmother's village. It has snow all year and the best sunsets in the world. "One day," she says, "I'll climb the highest mountain." Sven says, "Maybe we can go together." Nora smiles.
slides.pt: O livro de montanhas de Nora lista picos famosos.

slides.title: Superlativos
slides.rule: Use the antes do superlativo: the biggest, the best, the most beautiful. Irregulares: good → best, bad → worst.

slides.note: The + adjetivo + est (curto) ou the most + adjetivo (longo).

slides.title: Recordes do mundo
slides.text: O Guinness World Records registra os maiores e mais curiosos recordes do mundo. Em inglês: 'the biggest pizza', 'the longest hair', 'the fastest runner'. Um recorde é 'a record' e quebrar é 'to break a record'.
